8 احتفز He urged, or pressed forward, and strove, in his gait, or pace; (IAar, K;) [and so ↓ تحفّز : see الدَّوَالِيكُ, in art. دلك; and دَوَالَيْكَ, in art. دول.] ―
-b2- He sat upright, not in an easy posture; syn. اِسْتَوْفَزَ; as also ↓ تحفّز . (K.) [See the part. n., below.] ―
-b3- He drew himself together (تَضَامَّ) in his prostration and sitting. (K.) It is said in a trad. of 'Alee, إِذَا صَلَّتِ المَرْأَةُ فَلْتَحْتَفِزْ When the woman prays, let her draw herself together in her sitting and prostration, (S, Mgh, * TA,) and not put her arms apart from her sides, like the man. (S, TA.) ―
-b4- He settled himself in a sitting posture upon his buttocks: (En-Nadr, K:) or upon his knees, as though he would rise: (TA:) or he was uneasy, and raised himself, being vexed, or disquieted by grief: (IAth:) or he desired to rise and to lay violent hands upon a thing, while sitting. (TA.)
From An Arabic-English Lexicon (Edward William Lane)
